source.note:
EIGHT ISSUERS, EIGHT DOCUMENTS, NO COMMON PUBLISHER: DBS Bank Ltd (yuu Card, Woman's Card), Citibank Singapore Ltd (Rewards 10X), HSBC Bank (Singapore) Ltd (Revolution), United Overseas Bank Ltd (Lady's Solitaire), and DBS/POSB (PAssion). Two further programmes the household cares about — UOB PRVI Miles and Citi PremierMiles — have no primary source in this row at all; every encoded answer about them is Unconfirmed for that reason, not because the cards were judged unimportant. A ninth, Standard Chartered Smart, was never fetched and is absent from the domain's Card enum entirely.

Retrieved 2026-09-21 by the encoding session named in this row's NOTES.md. Full per-document provenance (URL, retrieval date, sha256, currency statement quoted verbatim) is in encodings/legalese/registers/source-bundle.json. The PDFs themselves are NOT vendored here (issuer copyright; redistribution terms unconfirmed) — the pdftotext extractions and the PDFs are held in legalese/l4-ide at jl4/examples/legal/miles-card/source/, commit 1dd165f9c and after, and are the authoritative copy this bundle pins against.

encodings_note: THE SUBJECT IS EIGHT INSTRUMENTS BY DIFFERENT PUBLISHERS, ENCODED AGAINST ONE SHARED ONTOLOGY, FILED AS ONE LEAF. This departs from docs/directory-conventions.md §3's rule that 'distinct instruments in a family are distinct leaves' — that rule's own worked case is a SAFE under two governing laws, i.e. the SAME instrument in two jurisdictions, which is a narrower fact pattern than eight DIFFERENT instruments by different issuers. The precedent this actually follows is subjects/sg/succession (four Acts, one shared family-law ontology, one leaf) and subjects/il/ofek-hadash-2008 (several collective agreements, one leaf) — both filed as bundles for the same reason this one is: the encoding's point is a comparison across the instruments (here, 'which card should I use for this purchase'), and a comparison has no home if its instruments are split across leaves that cannot reference each other. Meng ruled on the bundling shape 2026-09-21 (this row's own migration); the 'legalese' encoding's NOTES.md §1 states the argument in full so a later maintainer can disagree with it rather than reconstruct it. The 'payments' genre itself is new as of this row — see contracts/GENRES.md's entry for why none of the four seed genres held it.
